doc.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07

title: Which sisters played and with whom
summary: Billie goes through Edna, Mabel, Della, Sadie and Ida, who played church, house parties or bands, plus Ida's musician son.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Where I came from: parents, siblings and birth

blocks.x: Well, what about your other sisters? We got Ida and Sadie down, who they worked with over there some.
Well, Edna, she just worked for herself. It's by herself. You know, it's part. Parties, you know, Edna. Edna, she does. And, huh?
What is Edna in the office?
Huh?
What is Edna in the office?

Edna's in, she's in Florida. She's out there, she's out about, she's around a casino, I don't know, a casino or somewhere out there on the Gulf. She's working out there, you know, in a hotel out there. But she's not playing the music out there, she's working out there now. They said where she was when I was over there.
Well, now, you've got some other ones. Well, who's your older sister?
Sadie's oldest one living.

No, no more just playing for house parties, you know, amongst their friends and things like that. See, she didn't go around like me, like the rest of us, you know, playing for bands and things like that. She just played for house parties, you see. That's all.
See, we covered all six of them now? Something up in there? Della. Let's see.
Della? Della. Della, she played as my next older sister, see. Mabel was the oldest, then Della, then came Sadie, then Edna, then myself, then Ida.
Well, who did Della play with?

Della mostly just played for church. Church all the time. She mostly played for church all the time. She didn't care for, she would play in the ragtime, like houses like that, but she mostly spent her time in church, playing for church all the time. And Ida, she has a son, he's in the airport. He plays piano, and bass.
Three instruments he plays. What's his last name? Crumb, Danny Crumb. And he's around where?
Nah, he's in the, I don't even know where, wait, wait.
What's the ball in Texas out there? Wait a minute, I got a, he got a letter.

I'm in the river here. Yeah. I'm in the river here. I'm in the river here. I'm in the river here. I'm in the river here. I'm in the river here. I'm in the river here. I'm in the river here.

I'm in the river here outside. I'll give you a bite. Alright, fine.

I know, and, mate. That was when I went over to Florida, to meet his wife, you know? Uh-huh.
He plays with the Air Force man, huh?
Yeah.
